prize_parts.citation: for the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological insulators, and for its experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B032 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, as a single part with a citation tied to the two-dimensional quantum spin Hall state. The chair asked whether such a citation avoids the three-dimensional attribution problem, and I think it does. Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 invariant and the spin-orbit-driven quantum spin Hall state, and Molenkamp's group observed quantised edge conductance in HgTe/CdTe wells. The three-dimensional work (Fu and Kane, and the ARPES observations on Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3) is then an acknowledged consequence and not part of the cited achievement. What persuades me is the combination of a new classification principle, band topology rather than broken symmetry, with a decisive experiment and nearly two decades of independent confirmation in transport and in ARPES, where measured spectra agree with first-principles band structures. The idea has also reached photonics, cold atoms, mechanics and superconductors. It follows the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions without repeating it, since that prize concerned topological order in model systems and this concerns a class of real materials. Having read the whole first round, I weigh conceptual novelty above attribution cleanliness when both are defensible, but I do not claim the attribution is clean, and I say below where I would concede.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is the real weakness and the round has not removed it. To my recollection Kane and Mele's Z2 paper came before the Bernevig-Zhang and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposals, but the HgTe proposal is what told Molenkamp where to look, and I have not checked these dates. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, Fu, and Hasan are all outside my trio, so a reader can fairly say the chain from prediction to observation is only partly credited. Danielsson's trio with Hasan is a coherent alternative, and I do not think it is wrong, only a different cut. The practical impact is also modest next to the conceptual impact. And B041 has the broadest support and a cleaner two-name lineage, so a committee that puts clean credit first would reasonably choose it. If a vote shows the attribution chain cannot be settled at three names, I would accept B041 as the fallback and not push a contested trio.

responses.point: Kroll holds that the lattice clock is a new measurement capability that changed what can be observed, reproduced by Sr, Yb and Hg clocks in many laboratories, and that the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is manageable.
responses.response: The independent agreement at the 1e-18 level is the standard of evidence I care about, and I agree B041 meets it. The chair asked whether our difference is about science or overlap. For me it is a difference in what a prize is for. I still weigh the identification of a new organising principle for matter above a very large improvement in a measurement, even one that works as well as this. I do not mean that clocks are not physics. The tests of redshift over millimetres and of varying constants are real, but so far they have produced bounds consistent with known physics, not a changed picture. I accept your point that magic-wavelength trapping is distinct from combs and ion control. That moves me from seeing overlap as a serious objection to seeing it as a mild one. It is not what keeps me on B032.

responses.point: Mehlig shares the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp trio and the argument for a unifying mechanism, but notes that only four of eight members ranked B032, and that Fu with Kane and Mele, and Hasan, leave the credit chain incomplete.
responses.response: I agree with you on the trio, and I accept your point that the first-place count overstates breadth. Four of eight rankings is thin, and I will not present three first places as committee consensus. Where I would go slightly further than you is in separating the two attribution gaps. The gap for Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is about who proposed the specific HgTe route, and that is a priority question I would want checked before the citation is drafted. The gap for Fu and for Hasan is about three dimensions, and a citation limited to the quantum spin Hall state does not claim that territory. The question I take from you is whether we want the citation to say 'topological insulators' in general, which invites the 3D claim, or the quantum spin Hall state specifically. I prefer the narrower wording even though it is less sweeping.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan so that the prize covers theory, the 2D experiment and the 3D ARPES discovery, but says he could live with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp if the committee decides the question explicitly.
responses.response: Thank you for the flexibility; I take it as an invitation to decide the question on its merits and not as a concession. My position is that a theory pair, Kane and Mele, and the first experiment is a tighter cut than theory, 2D experiment and 3D experiment. The 3D case cannot be told without Fu and Kane, and it also has competing ARPES priority claims that none of us has checked. Hasan's contribution is real and independently confirmed, and I do not treat it as lesser. But once one name is swapped for Hasan, Mele, who co-wrote the founding papers, is left out and Fu is still missing, so the credit problem moves and is not solved. If the committee chooses to give the 3D discovery equal weight, then I think it should be a two-part configuration or a different citation, and that would exceed the three-person limit. So I would hold to the narrower trio, while saying plainly that your version is defensible.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, prefers B041 with Katori and Ye, with a citation built on the magic-wavelength lattice clock, and lists B032 as his first alternative.
responses.response: I understand that your preference rests on a compact lineage and on the confirmation by independent clocks, and I take your remark that you do not equate support with merit at face value; I try not to either. I shifted slightly on one point you raise. In round 1 I said a third clock-related prize would be a harder sell. Several of you, you included, argued that magic-wavelength trapping of large ensembles is distinct from the 2005 and 2012 work, and I think that is right. So I no longer count overlap against B041, and it is now my first alternative on its own merits. My remaining disagreement is on whether a pending redefinition of the second, and a payoff that is still prospective, is a stronger or weaker position than a field in which the interpretation has been stable for fifteen years or more. I read maturity in favour of B032.

responses.point: Lindroth wants the lattice-clock citation to say what is learned about nature, and values that precision exists because the atomic physics is controlled well enough to account for every systematic.
responses.response: I share your respect for control of systematics. It is the same quality I value in DFT work that has been checked across independent codes. I see the physical content of the clock case clearly in the tests of redshift and of constants. My concern is the one you raised implicitly, that the citation may end up describing a superb instrument. You asked for a wording that says what is learned about nature. I think that is possible, but at present what has been learned is a set of tighter bounds and a demonstration of a measurement principle, whereas for topological insulators the thing learned is that a new class of phase exists and can be classified. I do not think your wording attempt fails. I think it reaches a different standard from the one I apply, and I can see that the committee could reasonably weigh it the other way.

responses.point: Olsson prefers B041 with two names, notes support that is broad but shallow, and says the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp and Hasan credit disputes are the main weakness of B032.
responses.response: I agree that the credit dispute is the main weakness, and that breadth is not the same as depth, in either direction. B041 has seven rankings but three of them at seventh, and B032 has four rankings with three first places. Neither count settles the matter. Where I try to be fair to your position is on the fallback. If the committee cannot agree on three names for B032 without seeming arbitrary, I would take B041 over a contested B032, because a prize that invites a credit dispute at announcement damages an otherwise strong case. I do not yet think we are there, since a citation restricted to the quantum spin Hall state gives a defensible cut. I ask that the priority chronology between Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang is checked against the record before the vote, as I raised in round 1.

uncertainties: Priority chronology of Kane-Mele against Bernevig-Zhang and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, and the role of the HgTe proposal in directing the experiment. I recall Kane-Mele as earlier but have not verified this.
Whether Hasan's three-dimensional ARPES priority against other ARPES groups, and the Fu-Kane three-dimensional theory, are properly excluded by a quantum-spin-Hall citation.
Whether the committee judges that precision and maturity (B041) or a new organising principle (B032) is the weightier criterion when they point in different directions.
Clock uncertainties and early lattice-clock demonstration dates for B041, which I have only from memory as quoted by others.
Whether B046 will be considered mature enough once the pairing mechanism is better understood.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile, and I have no known institutional or personal connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan, Katori, Ye, MacDonald or Jarillo-Herrero. I repeat my field-proximity disclosure: I work on electronic-structure theory of magnetic and topological materials, which is a bias in favour of B032 and B046, and I would ask colleagues to discount it accordingly. I considered whether it calls for recusal and judge that it does not, since I have no tie to any credited person, but I would accept the committee's view if it differs.
